name: connect-databricks-export-prepare
description: What: Prepare the measured Databricks export (from the baseline): its own strategies when remote, the worker count from the parent, then drop and re-create the empty export target with its primary key. Run it through connect-databricks-export (reset + source data load + this), then the matching TestAuto workflow 'Connect Databricks Export <Size> <Threads>T'. Why: A building block of the Connect pack; a test, setup or schedule workload runs it so its steps exist once. When: Never run directly once the pack is tested; its parents run it. Running it alone is safe only when its own Needs are met. Needs: workloads it runs: connect-strategies-databricks-create; reference values: connect/databases:ProfiseeDatabaseName, connect/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName, connect/machines:ApplicationServerName, connect/machines:ApplicationServerNameFQDN, connect/machines:DatabaseServerName, connect/urls:ConnectBaseUrl. Success: Every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: Run connect-preflight first; then open the first failed step, whose If it fails text names what to check.
globalParametersNotes: SourceTableName comes from the parent; Size, RecordCount and Threads are the values of the run.

inputs.name: WorkerThreadCount
inputs.description: Worker thread count of the test (4, 8 or 12), passed by the 4T/8T/12T workload that runs this one.

inline.description: What: Make sure the Databricks export table exists with a primary key, then delete (when present), create and enable the Databricks strategies. Why: Runs the child workload 'connect-strategies-databricks-create' so its tested steps are reused here, not repeated. Success: The child workload ends with every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: Open the run output of 'connect-strategies-databricks-create'; its first failed step says what to check.

What: Set the Databricks service provider's Connect worker count to {{WorkerThreadCount}} (the last number of the run profile code). Why: Checks or changes the database directly, where the Profisee API has no call for it or a check must be exact. Success: The SQL finishes without an error; a THROW in the script fails the step with its own message. If it fails: Read the SQL error text first; then check the database server (connect/machines:DatabaseServerName) is reachable from this box with Windows authentication and the database named in the connection exists.

What: On the application server, find the Windows service of this Profisee instance (connect/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName, or the instance this workload targets): the service whose program lies in the installed Profisee folder that holds the instance's IIS application, never a typed name or a name prefix, because several instances and versions can share one server and the installer lets a person name the service anything. Only its short name is printed (nothing when the instance has none), into the run parameter InstanceServiceName that the service steps below read. Why: the service is stopped around a restore or a key change on releases that have one. Success: one name or nothing is printed; with nothing the service steps report Skipped, normal on releases without a Profisee Windows service. If it fails: the message says what was found: no IIS application for the instance (check the instance name in reference data), more than one service for the instance (names and programs listed: remove the stale one), or a service another instance in the same folder could own; or the admin credential (UserCredentials secrets) cannot reach the server over CredSSP.

What: Stop the Profisee Windows service on {{ApplicationServerName}} before IIS is stopped, recycled or restored under, so it holds no connection or cached state (skipped when this release has no Profisee Windows service). Why: Stop the Windows service so the next steps work on a quiet or a running Profisee instance, as they need. Success: The service on the target machine ends in the state the action asks for (Stop). If it fails: the admin credential (UserCredentials secrets) cannot manage services on that server over CredSSP, or the service did not reach the state in time (check it in services.msc there). Skipped when: the step Find The Instance Service found no Windows service for this instance, which is normal on releases without a Profisee Windows service.

What: Recycle the Connect service so it reads the worker count. The pools are found on the server at run time: the application pools that the IIS application /<instance>/api/connex use (whole path segments, so another instance whose name starts the same is never caught), never a typed list; recycle each of them. A built-in pool, or one that also serves something outside the instance, is never touched and is named in the output; the output lists every pool and what it serves. Why: Recycles or starts the IIS application pools so no service keeps caches from before a restore or a configuration change. Success: every pool found reaches Started. If it fails: the instance has no such IIS application on the server (check connect/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName, or the instance this workload targets, against IIS Manager), no pool may be touched, a pool did not reach Started within 120 seconds, or the admin credential (UserCredentials secrets) cannot reach the server over CredSSP.

What: Start the Profisee Windows service on {{ApplicationServerName}} after IIS is back, so it reads the current database and key (skipped when this release has no Profisee Windows service). Why: Start the Windows service so the next steps work on a quiet or a running Profisee instance, as they need. Success: The service on the target machine ends in the state the action asks for (Start). If it fails: the admin credential (UserCredentials secrets) cannot manage services on that server over CredSSP, or the service did not reach the state in time (check it in services.msc there). Skipped when: the step Find The Instance Service found no Windows service for this instance, which is normal on releases without a Profisee Windows service.

What: Call the gateway health check {{MainHealthUrl}} until every service reports Healthy (up to 10 minutes). A recycled service only starts on its first request; until then Monitor drains no messages and Connect batches get no activity rows. Why: Does work no single built-in step does (several calls, waits or checks in one place) and stops at the first problem. Success: The script finishes without an error; its output lines say what it did. If it fails: Read the last output line and the error text: the script names the value, server or record it could not handle.

What: Drop and re-create {{RemoteSchemaName}}.{{RemoteTableName}} empty, shaped like QA's {{RemoteShapeTableName}}, then add its primary key on {{ExportKeyColumn}} when it has none (Connect refuses an export table without one). Why: Does work no single built-in step does (several calls, waits or checks in one place) and stops at the first problem. Success: The script finishes without an error; its output lines say what it did. If it fails: Read the last output line and the error text: the script names the value, server or record it could not handle.
